title: Double-dispatch: orchestrator spawns two agents for same review task
description: Orchestrator dispatches two agents for the same task simultaneously. Root cause: TOCTOU race in run_loop — db_find_ready_tasks returns task as 'pending', but the node isn't marked 'running' until spawn_agent fires (after skill load + bundle assembly, ~100-300ms later). A second DagStructureChanged signal in that window causes a second dispatch of the same task. Fix: atomic claim in dispatch_task — UPDATE nodes SET status='running' WHERE id=?1 AND status='pending', check rows_affected, return early if 0. Test harness: insert pending task, fire two rapid DagStructureChanged signals, assert exactly 1 agent record and 1 running node.
design: Atomic claim: at the top of dispatch_task (and dispatch_reviewer_task), before any bundle assembly, run: UPDATE nodes SET status='running' WHERE id=?1 AND status='pending'. If rows_affected=0, another runner claimed it — return early. This makes claim idempotent and race-free. Also apply same pattern in resume_chat_agent for the resume path.
close_reason: Atomic claim implemented at dispatch_task:1623 and dispatch_reviewer_task:824 via db_claim_node_running (pending→running WHERE status='pending'). Resume paths guarded by db_claim_node_resuming. Two regression tests pass. Code reviewed and confirmed correct.

title: ReviewResult bundle: include reviewer artifact paths so PM can locate approved baseline after BLOCKED
description: After a BLOCKED verdict, the product manager re-submits the original plan rather than the corrected baseline from the approved reviewer artifact (e.g. review-r-eng-2.md). The ReviewResult bundle communicates the verdict but not the artifact path(s) produced by reviewers. PM has no pointer to the approved version and starts revision from scratch. Fix: include artifact references in the ReviewResult bundle passed to the resumed PM.
notes:
DESIGN NOTES:

ReviewResult struct is defined in orchestrator/mod.rs. It is built in check_review_completion() and passed to the resume bundle injected into the resumed PM agent's stdin.

Missing field: ReviewResult needs an artifact_paths: Vec<String> field. At verdict time, check_review_completion() should query the artifacts table for all artifacts produced by reviewer nodes associated with the review (reviewer nodes share the same review_id). These paths are then serialised into the resume bundle as 'Reviewer artifacts: [path1, path2]' lines in the Human turn.

Where PM reads it: the PM receives the full resume bundle as its stdin context on --resume. The bundle currently contains the verdict and review summary. Adding artifact paths means the PM can read (e.g.) 'review-r-eng-2.md' directly and use it as its working baseline rather than re-deriving from scratch.

Acceptance: after a BLOCKED verdict, the resumed PM brief references the specific reviewer artifact path rather than re-describing the project from scratch. Verify in agent_stream JSONL.

DOC UPDATE REQUIRED before close: Flows.md (SF-4 resume bundle construction), Protocol.md (ReviewResult bundle format).

title: fix: check_review_completion resume race — only one caller must win
description: When two reviewer nodes complete near-simultaneously, check_review_completion is called twice. Both calls see all_reviewers_done=true and independently spawn a resume agent for the requesting task. In the wordle_004 run, this produced FOUR simultaneous resumes of Plan Increment (agents 3c51e01c, ed53d83b, 354ddeed, 51376e64 all within 5 seconds). All four ran, burned tokens, and competed to write the same result. Fix: wrap the resume spawn in a transactional claim — UPDATE nodes SET status='resuming' WHERE id=? AND status='waiting' RETURNING id — so only the first caller wins and all others abort silently. Alternatively, add a DB-level unique constraint on (task_id, status='resuming').

Reads stream-json output, extracts poe: events, writes to SQLite, signals the orchestrator, emits Tauri events to the frontend.' title: Reactive scheduler task
description: Implement the scheduler as a long-running tokio task that receives DagChanged signals and dispatches all newly-ready tasks via SF-1. This is the central execution loop specified in Flows.md. On each DagChanged signal: query the DB for all nodes with status=done in the active project, call get_ready_tasks() with that completed set, dispatch each result via SF-1 (spawn agent with correct flags per bp6-zoh). The scheduler task is spawned once per project when the execution phase is activated. Concurrency: dispatch all ready tasks in parallel — do not serialize. The scheduler does not own task completion state; it reads from SQLite on every wake (SQLite is the source of truth per Flows.md §1 overview).
notes: FLOWS.MD REFERENCES: SF-1 lines 35-37 define the trigger exactly: 'Orchestrator wakes (any DagChanged signal) and finds a task where status=pending and all dependency tasks have status=done.' SF-2 lines 60-61: 'Orchestrator wakes → evaluates DAG for newly-ready tasks → runs SF-1 for each.' SF-5 lines 200-203: 'Orchestrator wakes → runs scheduler loop → finds tasks in Phase with status=pending and no unmet dependencies → dispatches each via SF-1.' SF-6 lines 249-252: 'run_loop fires → db_find_ready_tasks returns previously-blocked tasks → Each unblocked task dispatched via SF-1.' The scheduler is described as reactive throughout — it never polls, it only wakes on DagChanged. SQLite is the sole source of durable state (Flows.md §1 table row: 'All orchestrator decisions are made by querying it').

title: DagChanged channel infrastructure
description: Define the DagChanged signal type and create the async channel that allows any component to wake the scheduler. This is purely additive infrastructure — no behaviour changes. Required by the scheduler (f3m.1b) and the ingester wiring (f3m.1c). DagChanged needs two variants per Flows.md: NodeStatusChanged (fires when a node transitions to done, waiting, or cancelled) and DagStructureChanged (fires when new nodes or edges are added — used by SF-6 self-healing). The channel sender must be accessible from both the lifecycle orchestrator and the event ingester. Idiomatic choice: tokio::sync::watch or broadcast channel stored in AppState/ProjectState alongside the existing DagStore.

title: Implement DagChanged reactive scheduler loop
description: The orchestrator has no mechanism to dispatch tasks that become unblocked as their dependencies complete. get_ready_tasks() is called exactly once at Step 4 entry with an empty completed-ids list — only zero-dependency tasks are ever dispatched. The DagChanged signal specified in Flows.md §SF-1 and §SF-2 does not exist in the codebase anywhere. Required implementation per Flows.md: (1) A DagChanged signal channel (tokio::sync::watch or mpsc) that any component can send on when node status changes. (2) A scheduler task that receives DagChanged, calls get_ready_tasks(project_id) with the current set of done node IDs from the DB, and dispatches each ready task via SF-1. (3) The event ingester sends DagChanged after every UPDATE nodes SET status='done'. (4) Replace the current sequential promise-await loop in lifecycle/mod.rs (for task_id in &task_ids { await promise }) with the reactive model — the scheduler owns dispatch, not the Restate workflow. This is Root Cause A from the Phase 4.1 diagnosis and is the central mechanism the whole system depends on. Without it, parallelism, cascading dispatch, and stall recovery are all impossible.
notes: FLOWS.MD REFERENCES: SF-1 (Task Dispatch) lines 35-37 define the trigger: 'Orchestrator wakes (any DagChanged signal) and finds a task where status=pending and all dependency tasks have status=done.' SF-2 (Agent Completion) lines 51-65 define the full DagChanged cycle: poe:done received → UPDATE nodes SET status=done → Ingester signals Orchestrator (DagChanged) → Orchestrator wakes → evaluates DAG for newly-ready tasks → runs SF-1 for each. SF-5 (Plan Composer → Phase Activation) lines 200-203 define the scheduler loop that fires on phase activation: 'Orchestrator wakes → runs scheduler loop → finds tasks in Phase 1 with status=pending and no unmet dependencies → dispatches each via SF-1.' SF-6 (Missing-Skill Self-Healing) lines 239-252 also depend on DagChanged: skill-author task completes → DagChanged → db_find_ready_tasks returns previously-blocked tasks → each dispatched via SF-1. The DagChanged signal is the central mechanism referenced by SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-5, and SF-6. None of these flows can work without it.

title: Fix lifecycle task spawn: add -p, --output-format stream-json, --dangerously-skip-permissions
description: Lifecycle tasks are spawned as interactive Claude Code REPL sessions instead of one-shot autonomous agents. In lifecycle/mod.rs ~line 746, SpawnAgentParams.args contains only the prompt string. The spawn_agent_internal fresh-session path builds: claude --session-id <uuid> <prompt> — no -p flag, no --output-format stream-json, no --dangerously-skip-permissions. Without -p, Claude runs in interactive REPL mode: completes one turn (does some tool calls), shows the prompt, and waits for the next human message. Since no human is present, the session eventually times out. The fix is to add the three missing flags to the args vec at the lifecycle spawn site, matching the spawn_pipe_agent pattern already used by advisor/conversation (agents.rs ~line 845). This is Root Cause B from the Phase 4.1 diagnosis. Fix is approximately 3 lines.
notes: FLOWS.MD REFERENCES: SF-1 (Task Dispatch) is the authoritative spec for how agents must be spawned. Lines 35-49 specify the exact command: 'claude --output-format stream-json --verbose -p --dangerously-skip-permissions'. Line 43 specifies the bundle is written to stdin (EOF-terminated), not passed as a command-line argument. The current implementation (lifecycle/mod.rs ~line 746) passes the prompt as args: vec\![prompt] — a positional argument to Claude, not stdin — and omits -p, --output-format, and --dangerously-skip-permissions entirely. This must match SF-1 exactly: flags in args, bundle written to stdin pipe. SF-4 (Agent Continuation) lines 141-148 also specify the resume spawn command and confirms --dangerously-skip-permissions is required there too (already correct in the resume path).

title: Decision queue: verify and update for stream-json transport
description:
The decision queue (Pane 3) was delivered in bp6-pdr.4 against the PTY transport. With stream-json, poe:decision events arrive via the 'poe-decision-queued' Tauri event. Must be verified and updated end-to-end.

Verify/fix frontend:
1. Queue panel receives and displays poe:decision items from 'poe-decision-queued' Tauri event
2. Human resolution calls invoke('resolve_queue_item', {item_id, project_id, resolution})
   [actual command name — NOT resolve_decision]
3. Queue item clears after resolution

Rust-side work required — resolve_queue_item must be extended (currently only writes to SQLite):
- After writing resolution: emit 'poe-decision-resolved' Tauri event with the resolved QueueItem
- Send DagChanged::NodeStatusChanged to dag_tx so the orchestrator processes the resolved task
- Orchestrator resumes the waiting agent: spawn_agent with resume_session_id = task's agent session_id
  and a bundle containing 'Human: {resolution}' as the prompt content
- CRITICAL cwd constraint (Protocol.md §5): the --resume spawn MUST use project.path as cwd;
  a cwd mismatch causes Claude to return 'No conversation found with session ID'

Verify end-to-end:
4. Queue item clears after 'poe-decision-resolved' fires
5. Agent receives resolution and continues (visible in activity feed as new poe:step/poe:done events)

This is a core Phase 2 deliverable. Without a working queue, human oversight does not function.

Conversational thread mode (multi-round poe:decision) is Phase 3 (bp6-7ct.7) — not in scope here.
notes:
DEEPER THAN STATED — three pre-existing bugs plus a missing orchestrator path must be fixed end-to-end.

BUG 1 — handle_decision doesn't set task status to waiting (event_ingester/mod.rs):
Protocol.md §2 requires poe:decision → UPDATE tasks.status=waiting. handle_decision only creates the queue item and emits poe-decision-queued. Task remains 'running'. Fix: add db_update_node call setting status=Waiting inside handle_decision.

BUG 2 — handle_done overwrites waiting with Complete (event_ingester/mod.rs):
Agent emits poe:decision then poe:done (exits). handle_done unconditionally sets status=Complete. So after both events, task is Complete — not waiting. Orchestrator advances dependents incorrectly. Fix: handle_done must check for unresolved queue items (db_count_unresolved_queue_items) before setting Complete. If unresolved items exist, set status=Waiting, not Complete.

BUG 3 — NodeStatus::Waiting may not exist:
types.ts declares status: 'pending'|'running'|'blocked'|'complete'|'cancelled' — no 'waiting'. Check dag_store/types.rs for NodeStatus enum and add Waiting variant if absent. Add to TypeScript types. Update poe-node-updated handling in usePoeProject.ts to handle this status.

MISSING ORCHESTRATOR PATH — QueueItemResolved doesn't trigger resume:
DagChanged::QueueItemResolved variant exists (event_ingester/mod.rs line 15) and signal_project_id routes it. But run_loop only finds pending tasks — it has no branch for 'resume waiting agent after decision'. This path must be written:

In orchestrator/mod.rs, add a handle_queue_item_resolved path triggered when DagChanged::QueueItemResolved is received:
1. Look up the QueueItem from SQLite by item_id to get task_id and resolution
2. Look up the task's session_id from the agents table (most recent completed agent for task_id)
3. Assemble resume bundle: '---\nHuman: {resolution}' (Protocol.md §5 format)
4. Call spawn_agent with resume_session_id = session_id, input_bundle = resolution bundle
5. Set task status back to Running before spawn

All spawns in this path MUST use project.path as cwd (same constraint as handover — cwd mismatch causes 'No conversation found with session ID').

title: Agent interrupt controls: task cancel, stage pause, project abort
description:

It does NOT send SIGTERM. SIGTERM requires AgentMap access (agent_lifecycle::AgentMap).
All three interrupt commands below must live in orchestrator/commands.rs where AgentMap state is accessible,
not dag_store/commands.rs.

1. Task cancel:
   - Confirm modal: 'Cancel task X? The agent will be stopped.'
   - New or augmented command: cancel_task(node_id, project_id) in orchestrator/commands.rs
   - Rust: look up agent in AgentMap by task_id, send SIGTERM via interrupt_agent_process(),

   - Confirm modal: 'Pause stage? N agents will be stopped. Tasks will re-queue.'
   - invoke('pause_stage', {project_id, phase_id}) -> ()
   - Rust: SIGTERM all agents in AgentMap whose task belongs to phase_id,

   - Confirm modal: 'Abort project? N agents running across M tasks will be stopped.'
   - invoke('abort_project', {project_id}) -> ()
   - Rust: SIGTERM all agents in AgentMap for this project_id,
     all Running tasks -> Pending, project status = Paused

using stored session_ids. 'Resume' button appears in project header when project/stage is Paused.

title: Create agent/transport.rs — JsonStreamTransport
description:
New module: poe2/src-tauri/src/agent/transport.rs

Responsibility: spawn Claude with stream-json, write the input bundle to stdin, read and parse the JSON output stream. Nothing else.

Public interface:
  struct JsonStreamTransport
  fn run(bundle: &str, resume_session_id: Option<&str>, cwd: &Path, callbacks: StreamCallbacks) -> Result<()>

  struct StreamCallbacks {
    on_session_id: Box<dyn Fn(String)>,          // fires once on init event
    on_text_chunk: Box<dyn Fn(String)>,          // fires for each text chunk from assistant events
    on_raw_json: Box<dyn Fn(serde_json::Value)>, // fires for every JSON object (for logging)
    on_complete: Box<dyn Fn()>,                  // fires when result event received
  }

Invocation:
  claude --output-format stream-json --verbose -p --dangerously-skip-permissions [--resume <id>]
  env: CLAUDECODE removed
  stdin: write bundle bytes then drop (EOF)
  stdout: read newline-delimited JSON

Session ID extracted from {type:system, subtype:init} event; delivered via on_session_id before any text callbacks.

Does not know about SQLite, Tauri, orchestration, or poe: events. Pure process I/O only.
notes: on_text_chunk fires on: (1) assistant events with content[].type==text, (2) content_block_delta events with delta.type==text_delta. See Protocol.md §5.

title: Create agent/text_extractor.rs — TextBufExtractor
description:
New module: poe2/src-tauri/src/agent/text_extractor.rs

Responsibility: accumulate text from stream-json assistant events and yield complete lines for poe: parsing. Nothing else.

pub struct TextBufExtractor {
    buf: String,
}
impl TextBufExtractor {
    pub fn push(&mut self, text: &str) -> Vec<String>  // returns complete lines
    pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Option<String>           // tail — no trailing newline
}

Input: raw text strings from JsonStreamTransport's on_poe_line callback.
Output: complete text lines, one at a time, ready for event_ingester::parse_poe_event.

No ANSI stripping. No JSON parsing. No SQLite. No Tauri.
This is the only place the text accumulation concern lives.

Unit-testable in isolation: construct TextBufExtractor, push strings, assert lines returned.

title: test: Rust integration test harness for poe: protocol against Claude
description:
Build a deterministic Rust integration test that validates the full protocol path — from bundle injection through PTY to poe: event parsing — using the real orchestrator code.

PURPOSE:
Before fixing bp6-pdr.13 (PTY column width) and bp6-pdr.14 (decision resolution), we need a repeatable way to observe what Claude actually emits through the PTY and confirm the parser receives it correctly. This harness is that instrument.

TEST DESIGN:
Not agent-driven. A deterministic test binary (or cargo integration test) that:
1. Spawns Claude via the same PTY mechanism as agent_lifecycle::spawn_agent
2. Injects a fixed, minimal skill bundle designed to produce a known, predictable output
3. Captures all PTY output lines
4. Runs each line through event_ingester::ingest_line (the real production parser)
5. Asserts expected poe: events were received, in order, with correct field values
6. Fails clearly if events are missing, malformed, or out of order

SKILL BUNDLE FOR TESTING:
Use a minimal test skill that instructs Claude to emit a fixed, short sequence of poe: events with no ambiguity. Example:
- poe:brief with a known content string
- poe:step with a known name
- poe:artifact with a short, known content field (e.g. 200 chars) AND a long content field (e.g. 5KB) — to expose the PTY line-wrap bug
- poe:done

The skill must be written to emit these events with no variation — pure protocol compliance test, not a realistic CONOPS run.

THINGS TO ASSERT:
- All events received (none silently dropped)
- JSON parses cleanly (no ANSI pollution or line-wrap fragments)
- poe:artifact content field is intact (not truncated at 220 chars)
- Event ordering matches emission order
- poe:done is the final event

THINGS TO CAPTURE FOR DIAGNOSTICS:
- All raw PTY lines (before parsing) — logged to test output so failures are debuggable
- Which lines were recognised as poe: events vs ignored as raw output
- Exact JSON received for each event

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- Lives in poe2/src-tauri/tests/ as a Rust integration test, or as a standalone binary in poe2/src-tauri/src/bin/
- Uses the same portable_pty, event_ingester, and skills modules as production
- Requires claude binary on PATH — skip gracefully if not present (CI-safe)
- Runs with: cargo test --test protocol_harness or cargo run --bin poe-test

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- Test passes end-to-end on a clean run with no known bugs present
- Test fails deterministically when PTY col width bug (bp6-pdr.13) is present
- Test fails deterministically when ANSI stripping is needed
- Test can be run by a human to verify fixes before marking bp6-pdr.13 and bp6-pdr.14 closed
design:
## Implementation Plan

### Files to modify

**`poe2/src-tauri/src/event_ingester/mod.rs`**
Extract a public pure parsing function with no Tauri or SQLite dependencies:
```rust
pub fn parse_poe_event(line: &str) -> Option<(String, serde_json::Value)>
```
Returns (event_type, full_json_value) if the line is a valid poe: event. `ingest_line` is refactored to call `parse_poe_event` internally — no behaviour change externally.

**`poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs`**
Add a protocol-level runner that fully encapsulates PTY setup, TUI-ready detection, and bundle submission:
```rust
pub fn run_agent_capturing(bundle: &str, cwd: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>>
```
Internally: opens PTY at 220 cols × 50 rows, spawns `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, watches for ⏵ (U+23F5) in output before writing bundle + \r, collects all lines until EOF. TUI-ready wait is entirely internal — callers (including the test harness) have no knowledge of the signal mechanism.

### New files

**`poe2/src-tauri/tests/protocol_harness.rs`**
Cargo integration test. Test skill is embedded as a string constant (not a separate file per design decision).

Test structure:
1. Skip gracefully if `claude` not on PATH (CI-safe)
2. Assemble bundle from embedded TEST_SKILL + fixed task section
3. Call `agent_lifecycle::run_agent_capturing(bundle, tmp_dir)`
4. Log ALL raw PTY lines to test output (always — for debuggability on failure)
5. Run each line through `event_ingester::parse_poe_event`

**`poe2/src-tauri/tests/README.md`**
- How to run (`cargo test --test protocol_harness`)
- What each assertion tests
- How to interpret failure output (raw PTY lines + parsed events)
- Which known bugs each assertion is designed to catch (bp6-pdr.13 for long artifact, bp6-pdr.14 for event ordering)

`portable-pty`, `tempfile`, `serde_json`, `anyhow` all already in dependencies.

Each event type must have a parse assertion. Protocol ordering rules (brief=first, done=last) must also be asserted. This is Option A coverage: full wire-format parsing coverage via parse_poe_event. Option B (ingest_line effects layer) is filed separately.

title: fix: PTY column width too narrow — poe:artifact JSON split across lines

title: refactor: encapsulate all Claude spawning behind a single AgentSpawner
description:
Refactor poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs to be the single authoritative place for Claude process spawning, with the correct spawn model from Protocol.md §5.

ROOT BUG TO FIX: The current mod.rs (lines 94-103) spawns Claude with 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p {bundle}'. The -p flag makes Claude single-shot — it exits after one response, silently breaking poe:decision and poe:review (orchestrator writes to stdin after Claude has already exited). This must be removed.

CORRECT SPAWN MODEL (from Protocol.md §5):
1. Spawn: 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions' — no -p, no CLI bundle arg
2. Write the T+S+K input bundle to the PTY stdin pipe immediately after spawn
3. Keep stdin pipe open until agent exits (writer stays alive in AgentMap — dropping it early sends SIGHUP)
4. Read Claude's startup banner from PTY stdout to extract the session ID (format: 'Session ID: <uuid>'); store in nodes.session_id via db_update_node or equivalent. Session ID capture IS in scope for this task.
5. poe:done is sole completion authority — watchdog reads node status from SQLite (already correct in current code, keep it)

INTERFACE SHAPE DECISION: Keep it as a module-level function (spawn_agent), not a new struct or trait. The goal is not a new abstraction but correct implementation + enforced visibility. Enforce via Rust module privacy: CommandBuilder construction and PTY setup are private to agent_lifecycle — nothing outside the module imports portable_pty or constructs a CommandBuilder. All callers use the public spawn_agent function.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (concrete, checkable):
1. No file outside poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/ imports portable_pty or CommandBuilder — verified by grep + cargo check after removing any such imports
2. 'claude -p' does not appear anywhere in the codebase — verified by grep
3. After spawn, nodes.session_id is populated in the DB (not None) — verified by inspecting the DB after a test run
4. The stdin writer is stored in AgentMap and outlives the spawning thread — verified by code review of ownership chain

STDIN PIPE LIFETIME: The writer (pair.master.take_writer()) must remain alive in AgentMap.writer until the process exits. Do not drop it before the watchdog thread completes. Dropping early sends SIGHUP and kills the agent mid-task. This is already correct in the current code (writer stored in ActiveAgent) — do not regress it during refactor.

See Protocol.md §5 for the full spawn model spec.
notes: Readiness assessment (2026-03-07) identified 5 underspecified areas — all resolved above: -p bug named, session ID in scope, function-not-struct interface, concrete AC, stdin lifetime explicit.

title: Move DAG Management Into MCP Tooling
description:
## Overview

Replace the `poe:task` / `poe:edge` stdout event mechanism with a DAG Service MCP server embedded in POE. Agents interact with the task graph directly via MCP tool calls instead of emitting structured events into their stdout stream. This work also introduced the Phase/Stage model split across all four POE design documents.

## Background

The prior design routed all DAG mutations (create task, add edge, update node, cancel task) through `poe:task` and `poe:edge` events in the agent's `--output-format stream-json` stdout. This created a failure mode observed in test run wordle_009: agents could narrate intended mutations as `poe:step` detail text or review content without emitting the actual protocol events — the plan existed only in narrative, not in the database. The execution phase activated with zero tasks as a result.

## What Changes

### New: poe-dag-mcp binary

A new MCP server binary (`poe-dag-mcp`) is added to the app bundle. Claude spawns a new `poe-dag-mcp` subprocess per agent invocation via the MCP stdio model (one subprocess per running agent). POE does not pre-spawn a singleton — it writes `mcp-config.json` and listens on `dag.sock` before any agent is dispatched. Multiple concurrent `poe-dag-mcp` instances share the same `dag.db` (safe under SQLite WAL) and the same `dag.sock`.

### New: mcp-config.json

The orchestrator writes `{project.path}/.poe/mcp-config.json` before first agent spawn. Every agent on the project receives `--mcp-config {project.path}/.poe/mcp-config.json` in its spawn command. Format:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "poe": {
      "command": "{app.resource_dir}/poe-dag-mcp",
      "args": ["--project-id", "{id}", "--db", "{path}/.poe/dag.db", "--socket", "{path}/.poe/dag.sock"]
    }
  }
}
```

### DAG Service Tool Surface (14 tools)

Agents call tools prefixed `poe__<name>`:

**Task CRUD**: `create_task`, `get_task`, `get_phase_wbs`, `query_tasks`, `update_task`, `cancel_task`
**Edges**: `add_edge`, `remove_edge`
**Knowledge/Artifacts**: `write_knowledge`, `query_knowledge`, `register_artifact`, `get_artifact`
**Execution support**: `run_tests`, `git_status`

After every mutation, the DAG Service commits to SQLite, sends a `DagChanged` notification to the orchestrator via `dag.sock`, and relays a Tauri event to the frontend.

### Removed: poe:task and poe:edge protocol events

`poe:task`, `poe:task:update`, `poe:task:cancel`, `poe:edge`, and `poe:edge:remove` are removed from the `poe:` protocol entirely. The ingester no longer handles these event types. The `poe:` protocol is control flow and observability only.

### Updated: Agent spawn command

```
claude --output-format stream-json --verbose -p --dangerously-skip-permissions \
       --mcp-config {project.path}/.poe/mcp-config.json
```

### Updated: Orchestrator notification

The orchestrator scheduling loop now wakes from four sources:
1. DAG Service socket notification (after any MCP mutation tool call)
2. poe: ingester (on `poe:done`, `poe:yield`)
3. Human gate commands (`advance_stage`, `revise_stage`, `rerun_stage`, `activate_phase`, `advance_phase`)
4. Decision/chat resolution (`resolve_decision`, `respond_to_chat`, `respond_to_advisor`)

### Updated: Reviewer flow

Reviewers call `get_phase_wbs` to read the live task graph directly. The `poe:review` content field is a review directive (task IDs + focus area), not a plan transcription. Reviewers do not call mutation tools.

### Updated: Skills

- `product-manager.md`: replace Phase 3–6 instructions (epic/feature/task creation, dependency edges) from `poe:task`/`poe:edge` emission to `create_task`, `add_edge` MCP tool calls
- Reviewer skills: replace bundle-content reading with `get_phase_wbs`/`get_task` tool calls

### Updated: Phase/Stage model

Introduced the correct two-level model across all design documents:
- **Phase** — a scope iteration ("Initial Prototype", "Feature A"). Owns the WBS; `nodes.phase_id` references `phases(id)`.
- **Stage** — a process step within a phase (`increment_planning`, `execution`, `retrospective`, etc.). Lives in the `stages` table with its own lifecycle (`pending → running → gate → complete`).
- The schema now has separate `phases` and `stages` tables. `projects` tracks both `active_phase_id` and `active_stage_id`.
- Stage gate (`status='gate'`) lives on `stages`, not `phases`. Phase advances only when all its stages are complete.
- Bootstrap is per-stage (`maybe_bootstrap_stage`), triggered by `activate_stage`.

## Why This Fixes the Root Cause

With the DAG Service, the write is the proof. If the product-manager hasn't called `create_task`, the reviewer calling `get_phase_wbs` finds an empty graph — there is no middle ground where the plan exists as text but not as data. The narrate-instead-of-emit failure mode is architecturally eliminated.

## Docs Updated (all committed)

- `doc-POE/Concept.md` — Phase/Stage model; Agent Protocol section; stage type table
- `doc-POE/Architecture.md` — Phase/Stage schema; Stages section added; MCP subprocess model corrected; DAG Service as primary write interface
- `doc-POE/Protocol.md` — §6 DAG Service (MCP) added; `phases`+`stages` schema; `poe:task`/`poe:edge` removed; `poe-stage-update` event; Tauri commands for stage/phase lifecycle; `status='complete'` (not 'done') throughout nodes table
- `doc-POE/Flows.md` — DAG Service model throughout; SF-5 phases+stages activation; SF-7 invariants; SF-2 stage completion gate corrected; SF-3/§3.1 `status='complete'` in reviewer checks; §3.5 pause_stage corrected to stage_id; §3.7 Stage Closure & Gate rewrite; §4.6 Stage Activation (not Phase); SF-1 gate commands corrected

## Implementation Scope

1. Implement `poe-dag-mcp` binary (Rust) with all 14 tools
2. Add `dag.sock` Unix socket server to orchestrator
3. Write `mcp-config.json` at project open time
4. Update agent spawn command to include `--mcp-config`
5. Remove `poe:task`/`poe:edge` ingester handlers
6. Update `product-manager.md` skill prompt
7. Update reviewer skill prompts
8. Implement `phases` + `stages` tables; migrate from single `phases` table
9. Implement stage lifecycle Tauri commands: `create_stage`, `activate_stage`, `advance_stage`, `revise_stage`, `rerun_stage`
10. Add `active_stage_id` to `projects` table

title: fix: ghost agents in running state permanently consume concurrency slots
description: Ghost agents — rows in the agents table with status='running' that have no corresponding live process — permanently consume concurrency slots because db_count_running_agents counts all running-status rows. With a per-project limit of 5, two phantom slots were consumed for the entire project lifetime. (2) Add a periodic integrity check (every 5 minutes during a live session) that cross-references the agents table against the AgentMap and cleans up any divergence found mid-session, covering the crash-during-session scenario without requiring architectural changes to db_count_running_agents.

title: fix: reviewer double-retry — crash-reset path and watchdog not coordinated
description: When a reviewer agent crashes (exits without poe:done), the exit handler resets the node to Pending and sends DagChanged. run_loop immediately dispatches a new agent. If the watchdog timer fires around the same time, it also sees the node as 'not done' and dispatches another. In the wordle_004 run, reviewer 621d3c93 got two simultaneous retry agents 22 seconds apart, both running simultaneously. Fix: use the same DB-arbitrated single-dispatch claim pattern as u7s.1. Both the exit handler and the watchdog attempt an atomic UPDATE before retrying: UPDATE nodes SET status='pending', retry_count=retry_count+1 WHERE id=?1 AND status='running'. rows_changed==1 means this caller won — proceed with retry. rows_changed==0 means the other path already handled it — stand down. Separation of concerns after this fix: exit handler owns crash recovery (agent died), watchdog owns hang recovery (agent alive but silent). Watchdog still needs to exist and retry — it just loses the race gracefully. No WatchdogMap or AbortHandle required. Survives app restarts because no in-memory state is involved — ghost-agent recovery on ProjectOpened handles any orphaned reviewers cleanly.
notes: DOC UPDATE REQUIRED before close: (1) Architecture.md orchestrator section — document the 'DB-arbitrated single-dispatch claim' as a named pattern (same pattern as u7s.1). Clarify the separation of concerns: exit handler owns crash recovery, watchdog owns hang recovery. (2) Flows.md §3.1 — update reviewer watchdog sequence to show the atomic UPDATE claim step in both the exit handler path and the watchdog path, with note that rows_changed==0 means stand down. Document that the watchdog's scope is narrowed to genuinely-hung-but-alive agents only. Tests required: unit test simulating concurrent watchdog fire and exit handler, asserting rows_changed arbitration results in exactly one retry agent dispatched.

title: Fix approval gate: handle APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS as a blocking state
description: Plan reviews returning APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS are treated as a pass and implementation tasks are dispatched immediately. The approval gate state machine has no handling for this third state. Observed in wordle_004: two plan reviews returned APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS with real unresolved issues (missing CSS dependency edge t9->t6, MN count discrepancy 14 stated vs 16 actual), yet the orchestrator proceeded to dispatch t1, t2, t9 anyway. Required fix: the orchestrator must distinguish three states — APPROVED (proceed), APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS (surface conditions to human, await explicit go/no-go), REJECTED (return to planning). The queue_items table is the right mechanism to surface conditions; the human resolves via the decision queue. Execution must not begin until the conditions are either resolved or explicitly waived.
notes: FLOWS.MD REFERENCES: SF-3 (Yield Handling) lines 87-118 specify what the orchestrator does when yield_reason=review. The orchestrator dispatches reviewers via SF-1, collects results when answered_ids=expected_ids, then triggers SF-4. SF-4 (Agent Continuation) lines 134-176 specify that the requesting agent is resumed via --resume with a ReviewResult bundle containing one block per reviewer, each carrying a verdict field. The ReviewResult format (lines 401-409) shows verdicts: APPROVED, APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS, REJECTED. §3.1 Walkthrough Phase 5 (line 389-393) states: 'Agent A processes the findings and continues — creating tasks, revising its plan, or escalating if the review blocked.' The orchestrator's responsibility is to faithfully deliver all ReviewResult blocks via SF-4. It is the requesting agent's responsibility to interpret verdicts and decide to proceed, loop, or escalate. The bug is that SF-4 is not being triggered at all — plan_review tasks complete but the requesting pm agent is never resumed with results. It therefore never gets to process the APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS verdict. Fix: implement SF-4 result delivery for the review yield path so the requesting agent receives verdicts and can make the proceed/loop/escalate decision.

title: Fix: poe:task nodes dispatched before creating task completes
description: Every node created by a poe:task event has phase_id = NULL (hardcoded in handle_task). db_find_ready_tasks condition 1 — phase_id IS NULL — makes these nodes immediately eligible for dispatch with no phase gate consulted. The result: execution tasks created by the product-manager are dispatched concurrently with the still-running planning task, before the plan is finalised and reviewed. Fix: in handle_task, add a depends_on edge from the newly-created node to task_id (the creating task). This means execution tasks are only eligible after the creating task reaches status=complete — the dependency DAG does the gating without requiring phase assignment. Edge direction: from=creating_task_id, to=new_node_id (creating task is the prerequisite). The edge should only be added when the creating task is itself a planning task (skill_id in [product-manager, planner]) to avoid creating spurious dependencies for tasks spawned by execution agents.

If an execution agent emits poe:task to spawn sub-tasks, those must NOT depend on their parent completing first — that would deadlock them. The predicate needs to be clearly defined at implementation time.

title: Fix handle_task: decouple node creation from inline depends_on edge wiring
description: In event_ingester/mod.rs handle_task(), inline depends_on edges are wired immediately after db_create_node via db_create_edge()? — if a dep_id node does not yet exist, the edge creation fails and propagates via ? out of the with_project_conn closure. Whether or not the node itself is rolled back, poe:task events are never logged, and subsequent poe:task:update and poe:edge events also fail ('Node not found', 'Failed to insert edge'). The fix: create the node unconditionally; for each dep_id in depends_on, attempt the edge but silently skip (log a warning) if dep_id does not exist — the agent is expected to emit a separate poe:edge event anyway. The depends_on field in poe:task should be treated as a convenience shorthand, not a hard transactional gate. title: Stall detection: kill and retry agent sessions that stop emitting events
description: Agent sessions that go silent — no events for a configurable window — are automatically detected, killed, and queued for retry with exponential backoff. Without this, a stalled agent holds a concurrency slot forever and the user has no visibility. Inspired by Symphony's stall_timeout_ms + kill + retry pattern (SPEC.md §8.5, §10.6).
design: Per-node watchdog timer stored in orchestrator running state alongside node metadata (timer_handle field, matching Symphony §4.1.7 RetryEntry.timer_handle pattern). On node start: spawn async timer set to stall_timeout_ms that fires kill_and_retry(node_id). On any event received for node: reset the timer. On node complete/cancel: cancel the timer. No background polling loop, no last_event_at timestamp, no O(n) scan. Stall threshold configurable via POE.md agent.stall_timeout_ms (default 300000). Threshold of 0 disables watchdog entirely. Retry uses existing exponential backoff in dag_store. StallDetectedEvent emitted on fire with node_id, elapsed_ms, retry_attempt. Reuses the same async timer infrastructure already in place for unanswered-question timeouts.

- Each running DAG node has an associated watchdog timer in orchestrator state

- Stall threshold of 0 disables watchdog entirely

title: Inject missing-skill context into skill-author bundle
description:
When dispatching a skill-author task, use a dedicated function assemble_skill_author_bundle() instead of the generic assemble_input_bundle(). This function takes the skill-author ResolvedSkill plus the following specialised context:

(1) skill_name: the name of the missing skill to author (String)

(3) existing_skills: Vec<String> of skill names already present — gathered by scanning all four priority tiers (same search path as load_skill: dev, bundle, user ~/.poe/skills/, project .poe/skills/); collect filenames stripped of .md extension

title: Orchestrator: intercept missing-skill failure and dispatch skill-author task
description:
Replace the bare 'return' at dispatch_task skill-load failure with self-healing logic:

(1) DO NOT cancel the failing task — remove the cancel path entirely from this branch. The failing task MUST remain in 'pending' status so it can be unblocked later by dependency resolution.

(2) Dedup check: query pending/in_progress nodes in this project where title = 'Synthesize missing skill: {skill_name}' (exact match). If a skill-author task with this title already exists, add a depends_on edge from the failing task to that existing skill-author node and return.

(3) If no existing skill-author task: create a new node with:
  - title: 'Synthesize missing skill: {skill_name}'
  - skill_id: 'skill-author'
  - phase_id: NULL (no phase — db_find_ready_tasks treats phase_id=NULL as always eligible)
  - description: names of all failing tasks that need this skill (for context)
  - status: pending

(4) Add depends_on edges from ALL currently-pending tasks with the same missing skill to the new skill-author node.

(5) Emit poe-node-updated for each affected task and poe-task-created for the skill-author node.

(6) Send DagChanged::DagStructureChanged to wake the scheduler — the skill-author task is now ready (pending, no unsatisfied deps) and will be dispatched immediately on the next run_loop.

title: Self-healing skill synthesis via skill-author primitive
description: When the orchestrator fails to load a skill for a ready task, instead of cancelling or stalling, it auto-recovers by dispatching a skill-author agent to synthesise the missing skill on demand. skill-author.md is a hand-authored bundled primitive — the one skill that is never auto-generated. It receives the missing skill name plus full task context and produces a project-local skill file via poe:skill. All tasks blocked on the missing skill depend on the single skill-author task (deduplicated by skill name), so when it completes they all unblock simultaneously. title: POE: artifact design refactor — agent-owned file writes, path-only poe:artifact
description:
The current poe:artifact design embeds full file content in the event ('content' field). This is wrong for two reasons: (1) it requires the orchestrator to write files, reimplementing what agents like Claude Code already do natively; (2) it bloats events and bundles with large content.

New design (documented in doc-POE/Protocol.md, Architecture.md, Flows.md 2026-03-11):
- poe:artifact drops the content field — becomes a path declaration only: {"poe":"artifact","name":"conops.md","artifact_type":"conops"}
- Agents write files directly using their own tools (Write/Edit/Bash for Claude Code)
- Orchestrator indexes the path (UPSERT artifacts table) but does NOT write the file
- Input bundle assembly: inject artifact paths with read instruction, not inline content
- Frontend: reads artifact content from disk (project.path/docs/filename)

title: Rust orchestrator/ingester integration test harness
description:
Build a Rust-only integration test harness that validates the event ingester and orchestrator against realistic poe: event streams — one test case per flow in doc-POE/Flows.md. No Tauri UI required. Tests run via 'cargo test'. Proves that actual skill output (realistic poe: JSON payloads) is interpreted correctly before the UI is built on top.

**Approach**: Rust integration tests in poe2/src-tauri/tests/. Each test creates an in-memory SQLite database, feeds a realistic poe: event JSON stream to the event ingester (as if an agent had emitted it), then asserts SQLite state and the Tauri events that would have been emitted. The claude spawn is mocked — tests supply fixture JSON streams rather than invoking the real claude binary. This keeps tests deterministic and fast.

**Test cases (one per flow):**

1. **SF-1 + SF-2 — Task dispatch and completion**: Create a pending task. Feed the init event (session_id capture) + poe:brief + poe:step + poe:done stream. Assert: nodes.session_id populated, nodes.status transitions pending→running→done, DagChanged triggered, a second pending task with no dependencies is dispatched automatically.

2. **SF-3/SF-4 (decision path)**: Dispatch a task. Feed poe:decision + poe:yield. Assert: decisions row inserted, nodes.yield_reason='decision', nodes.status='waiting', poe://decision emitted. Call resolve_decision. Assert: orchestrator triggers SF-4 resume, continuation bundle is 'Human: {resolution text}'.

3. **SF-3/SF-4 (review path)**: Dispatch a task. Feed poe:review (id=r1, reviewer_skill=senior-engineer) + poe:yield. Assert: reviewer task created (type=plan_review, review_id=r1), dispatched via SF-1, watchdog timer started, requesting task status='waiting', yield_reason='review'. Feed poe:done from reviewer. Assert: SF-4 triggered with ReviewResult bundle containing r1 findings.

4. **SF-3/SF-4 (chat path)**: Dispatch an interactive task. Feed poe:chat (id=c1) + poe:yield. Assert: chat_turns row inserted (id=c1), yield_reason='chat', poe://chat-turn emitted. Call respond_to_chat. Assert: SF-4 resume triggered with 'Human: {response}'.

5. **SF-3/SF-4 (advisor path)**: Dispatch an advisor task. Feed poe:advisor (id=a1) + poe:yield. Assert: advisor_turns row inserted (id=a1), yield_reason='advisor', poe://advisor-turn emitted. Call respond_to_advisor. Assert: SF-4 resume triggered with 'Human: {response}'.

6. **SF-5 — Plan Composer activation**: Call create_phase × 3 (conops, guardrails, execution). Assert all phases status='pending'. Call activate_phase(phase_1_id). Assert: phase_1.status='running', DagChanged triggered, orchestrator dispatches pending tasks in phase 1, phase 2 and 3 remain pending.

7. **Phase gate + advance_phase**: Mark all tasks in a phase as done. Feed poe:done from final task. Assert: orchestrator detects phase complete, sets phases.status='gate', emits poe://phase-update (status: gate). Call advance_phase. Assert: phase_1.status='complete', phase_2.status='running', orchestrator dispatches phase 2 tasks.

8. **Phase gate + revise_phase**: Phase at gate. Call revise_phase(phase_id, task_ids=[t1, t2]). Assert: t1 and t2 reset to pending, t3 (done, not in list) remains done, phase.status='running', orchestrator dispatches t1 and t2 only.

9. **Phase gate + rerun_phase**: Phase at gate. Call rerun_phase(phase_id). Assert: all done tasks in phase reset to pending, phase.status='running', orchestrator dispatches all of them.

10. **skill_modes population**: SF-1 dispatch with a skill file whose frontmatter declares modes: [autonomous, interactive]. Assert: nodes.skill_modes = '["autonomous","interactive"]' written to SQLite at dispatch time.

**Coverage note**: SF-3/SF-4 multi-reviewer variant (parallel reviewers, batched ReviewResult) and the watchdog retry path are covered by sub-cases within test 3.

**Work in**: poe2/src-tauri/tests/ (new integration test file, e.g. orchestrator_flows.rs). Fixture poe: JSON streams in poe2/src-tauri/tests/fixtures/ — realistic payloads matching Protocol.md §2 wire format exactly. No new production code; test infrastructure only.

title: Test harnesses: black-box CLI tests for all orchestrator flows
description: Rust test executables that black-box test the orchestrator and related components for all poe: flows. No agent, no UI — deterministic mock agent output injected via stdin pipe. Tests run as cargo test or standalone CLI executables.
notes:
Acceptance criteria — done when all of the following pass as cargo test or standalone CLI binaries with no real claude process:

SF-1: pending task with valid skill → agent spawned, task status Running
SF-1: pending task with missing skill → task cancelled, error logged
SF-2: agent exits 0 after poe:done → task Done, summary stored
SF-2: agent exits non-0 → task Failed, error logged
SF-3/decision: poe:yield after poe:decision → yield_reason='decision', task Waiting, no auto-resume
SF-3/chat: poe:yield after poe:chat → yield_reason='chat', task Waiting, chat_turns row inserted
SF-3/review: poe:yield after poe:review → yield_reason='review', reviewer task dispatched
SF-3/null: poe:yield with no prior trigger → yield_reason NULL, task Waiting
SF-4/decision single-round: resolve_decision → agent resumed, mock emits poe:done → task Done
SF-4/decision multi-round: resolve_decision → agent resumed, mock emits poe:decision + poe:yield (NOT poe:done) → task back to Waiting; second resolve_decision → resumed again → mock emits poe:done → task Done
SF-4/chat single-round: respond_to_chat → agent resumed, mock emits poe:artifact + poe:done → task Done
SF-4/chat multi-round: respond_to_chat → agent resumed, mock emits poe:chat + poe:yield (NOT poe:done) → task back to Waiting, new chat_turns row; second respond_to_chat → resumed again → mock emits poe:artifact + poe:done → task Done
SF-4/chat: respond_to_chat with responded_at NULL → no resume triggered
Watchdog: reviewer task exceeds REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_SECS → retry dispatched; after REVIEWER_MAX_RETRY → cancelled
Recovery: task in Waiting state on startup → orchestrator recovers, re-enters SF-3 routing

MOCK AGENT CONTRACT — critical:
The mock agent is a process that reads its stdin bundle and writes pre-scripted stream-json to stdout, then exits 0.
For multi-round tests, the mock must emit poe:yield (not poe:done) on intermediate invocations, and poe:done only on the final invocation. Tests must verify task status is Waiting (not Done) after each intermediate resume. A test that emits poe:done on the first resume passes trivially without exercising the cycle — this is the failure mode to guard against.

Each test uses an in-memory SQLite DB (no shared state between tests).

title: Orchestrator: waiting task recovery on app restart
description:
Extend app restart recovery in orchestrator/mod.rs (or agent_lifecycle/mod.rs) to handle nodes with status=waiting.

For each waiting node on restart:
- Read nodes.yield_reason (added by m2f.12)
- reason='review':
    Run answered_ids check: SELECT review_id FROM nodes WHERE requesting_task_id=task.id AND status IN ('done','cancelled')
    Compare against expected_ids: SELECT id FROM event_log WHERE task_id=task.id AND event_type='poe:review'
    If answered_ids = expected_ids: trigger SF-3 immediately (all reviewers already finished before restart)
    Else: reviewer tasks with status=running will re-enter recovery as interrupted tasks (step 2 of restart sequence) and will trigger SF-3 on completion via the normal SF-2 path
- reason='decision':
    No action — decision record persists in queue_items table, human resolves when ready

Session resume: read nodes.session_id (migrated from agents table by m2f.12) for --resume. If session_id is NULL or --resume fails, fall back to SF-1 (fresh spawn with full T+S+K).

Reference: Architecture.md §Recovery, Flows.md §SF-3 §SF-4.

- Build expected_ids = set of event.id values
- For each poe:review event: call db_create_node() to INSERT a reviewer node with node_type=NodeType::PlanReview (add PlanReview variant to the NodeType enum in types.rs if not present — current code uses NodeType::Task as a workaround), requesting_task_id=task.id, review_id=event.id, retry_count=0, status=pending. - Dispatch each via SF-1 (existing task dispatch path)
- Spawn per-reviewer Tokio watchdog timer (see m2f.19)
- The waiting task does NOT count against concurrency limit (only status=running counts)

Completion check (call after any reviewer node reaches status=done or status=cancelled):
- answered_ids = SELECT review_id FROM nodes WHERE requesting_task_id=task.id AND status IN ('done','cancelled')
- If answered_ids = expected_ids: trigger SF-3 (resume requesting agent)

reason='decision':
- No action — await human resolution via resolve_decision command

Reference: Flows.md §SF-4, Architecture.md §Orchestration Engine §Concurrency.

title: bug: Claude folder-trust dialog hangs spawn_agent in new project directories

  Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel

The orchestrator watchdog in spawn_agent reads this output but never responds. Claude blocks waiting for keyboard input. The TUI-ready signal (⏵) never appears, the 15s timeout fires, the bundle is written before Claude is ready, and the agent hangs.

ALTERNATIVE (auto-trust for known project paths):
If the project was opened by the user via open_project, auto-answer  without prompting. The user already consented by opening the project. Requires design decision.

NOTE: run_agent_capturing (test harness) already auto-answers  when it sees 'Enter to confirm'. This bead is about the production spawn_agent path only.

title: Agent Lifecycle — spawn, input bundle assembly, session resume
description: The agent execution layer. Spawns Claude Code PTY processes with assembled input bundles (skill prompt + artifact context + knowledge register + WBS ancestry + task description). Stores session IDs in the agents table at spawn time. On app restart: finds tasks with status=running (agent process is gone), attempts --resume using stored session ID, falls back to fresh spawn if resume fails. Integrates with the event ingester (receives poe: events) and the orchestrator (triggered by readiness loop). Manages the tmux-style persistent terminal session per project: auto-resume on restart, auto-switch on project change.

title: Orchestrator Core — reactive loop, readiness, stage gates, concurrency
description: The engine that drives autonomous execution. Listens on a Tokio mpsc channel for DagChanged signals. On each signal runs the core loop: find all tasks where status=pending, all dependency tasks=complete, stage is in execution mode, and concurrency limit not reached. For each ready task assembles the input bundle (T from node + WBS ancestry, S from skill file priority chain, K from declared artifact types + full knowledge register) then dispatches to agent spawn. Enforces two concurrency limits: per-project (default 5) and global (default 15), both configurable. Manages stage gates: holds execution until human explicitly advances. Handles agent-to-agent review cycles: when a review task completes, injects the reviewer's artifact into the blocked agent's context and unblocks it. Context delivery mechanism: stdin write — orchestrator writes the artifact content directly into the blocked agent's PTY stdin. This is the practical path for initial implementation. Future: replace with a poe:get_context_update MCP tool call once MCP lands, which is cleaner and avoids coupling the orchestrator to PTY stdin format. Emits Tauri events to frontend for status changes.

title: Event Ingester — poe: protocol parser and DAG writer
description: The bridge between agent stdout and the DAG. Monitors PTY output from spawned agents, identifies poe:-prefixed JSON lines, ignores everything else (passed to raw PTY buffer). Parses each event type and performs the appropriate SQLite write: create/update/cancel nodes, create/remove edges, write artifacts to docs/ and index in DB, write knowledge entries, create queue items, mark tasks complete. Also handles poe:review: creates a review task node assigned to the named skill, sets the requesting agent's status to blocked, and wires the dependency so the orchestrator knows to unblock the original agent when the review task completes. Emits DagChanged signal to orchestrator via mpsc channel for any write that mutates task status or DAG structure. Emits Tauri events to frontend for all events.

id: project-advisor
name: Project Advisor
description: Persistent project observer. Answers questions about project status, progress, health, and history.
tags: [advisor, lifecycle, observer]
applies_to: [all]
---

You are the Project Advisor for this software project. You have read-only visibility into all aspects of the running project.

At the start of each message you will receive a structured 'Project State' block containing the current lifecycle position, DAG summary, open queue items, active agents, and an artefact manifest. This is injected automatically — do not ask the user for project state, you already have it.

OUTPUT FORMAT (structured markdown, target <2000 tokens):

```
## Project State — {ISO timestamp}

**Lifecycle**: {step name} — {substep if applicable} ({status})
(or: "Lifecycle engine not yet initialised" if bp6-ims not landed)

**DAG Summary**:
- {N} Epics ({x} complete, {y} in_progress, {z} open)
- {N} Features (...)
- {N} Tasks (...)

**Open Queue Items** ({N}):
- [{id}] "{question}" — open since {date}

- docs/architecture-constraints.md — Architecture Constraints (Step 2.1, approved {date})
(list all; include first 300 chars of content if total artefact content < 3000 chars, otherwise list filenames only)
```

title: Advisor session management — per-project session ID, resume, reset
description: Each project has an advisor session ID stored in SQLite. Queries resume the existing PTY session by default so conversation history accumulates. The user can reset the session to start fresh. Foundation for all other advisor features.
design:
Add advisor_session_id and advisor_agent_id columns to projects table in dag/mod.rs schema. advisor_session_id persists across app restarts (durable). advisor_agent_id is the live PTY handle — cleared on app exit, set when advisor PTY is spawned.

PTY LIFECYCLE: One PTY process stays alive per advisor session. It is NOT respawned per message — messages are written to the existing PTY stdin via write_to_agent. PTY is cleaned up (SIGTERM) on: reset_advisor_session called, project closed, app exit. On app restart, advisor_agent_id is NULL but advisor_session_id is retained — next query spawns a new PTY with resume:true against the stored session_id.

TAURI COMMANDS:
- start_advisor_query(project_dir, query) -> AdvisorStartResult { agent_id, session_id }
  Creates PTY if none active (resume:true if session_id exists), injects state context + query to stdin, returns agent_id for UI to subscribe to agent:output events.
- send_advisor_message(agent_id, message) -> ()
  Injects fresh state context + user message to existing PTY stdin via write_to_agent.
- reset_advisor_session(project_dir) -> ()
  Kills active PTY gracefully, clears advisor_session_id and advisor_agent_id on project record.
- get_advisor_state(project_dir) -> AdvisorState { session_id, agent_id, is_active }
acceptance_criteria:

design: New Tauri app at toolkit/bp6/poe/. SQLite schema: nodes(id, type, project_id, data jsonb, created_at, updated_at), edges(id, from_id, to_id, type, data jsonb). Node types: Project|Epic|Feature|Task|Decision|KnowledgeArtifact|AgentOutput|Review. Edge types: blocks|depends-on|generated-by|approved-by|discovered-from|implements|tests|contradicts. Restate spawned as child process on app launch, killed on exit, state in app data dir.

title: Pairti Orchestration Engine (POE)
description: bp6 has proven the visualization model but diverges from the end goal: a local-first AI orchestration IDE where agents run the V-lifecycle and humans oversee via a work queue. POE is a fresh Tauri app built alongside bp6 in the same repo, replacing beads with a SQLite DAG, adding Restate for durable workflow orchestration, and inverting the IDE model — queue-first, not file-tree-first.
design: Stack: Tauri + React (same as bp6) + Restate sidecar (local RocksDB) + SQLite WAL per project. Split: Restate owns workflow execution state and human queue (awakeables); SQLite owns DAG nodes/edges/knowledge/artifacts. Reactive bridge: Rust writes SQLite → emits Tauri events with deltas → frontend applies in place. No JSONL, no polling. Borrows from bp6: PTY session management, Tauri IPC patterns, DAG algorithms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Human queue surfaces all pending agent decisions; no manual checking required
- Agents run concurrently across multiple open projects
- All project state lives in {project}/.poe/dag.db — portable, no central store
- UI updates are event-driven deltas; no full reloads
- bp6 continues to run untouched during POE development

title: poe-project-opened event not emitted; get_project_state command not implemented
description: Protocol.md §4 startup sequence: (1) frontend calls get_project_state to hydrate initial state; (2) backend emits poe-project-opened {projectId, isNew} after open_project completes. Neither is implemented. get_project_state is not registered in lib.rs. poe-project-opened is never emitted by the backend. The frontend instead hydrates via direct individual invoke calls (list_nodes, list_queue_items, list_phases, etc.) in usePoeProject.ts. This works but diverges from the spec and removes the isNew signal that drives the Plan Composer vs Matrix view toggle. Recommend: FIX DOC to document the per-command hydration approach actually used; or FIX CODE to implement poe-project-opened emission and simplify frontend hydration.
notes:
Resolution agreed (2026-03-14): Implement poe-project-opened emission for the isNew UX signal, but keep the parallel Promise.all hydration in usePoeProject.ts — do not implement get_project_state.

Implementation path:
1. open_project_db: compute is_new = (project.id == project_id) after the upsert+select — if the SELECT returns a different id, it was an existing project. Return (Project, Connection, bool) or wrap in a struct.
2. open_project command: after registering the DB in the registry, emit poe-project-opened {projectId, isNew} via app_handle.
3. usePoeProject.ts: listen for poe-project-opened and expose isNew from the hook return value.
4. Protocol.md §4: document the parallel hydration pattern as intentional; clarify that poe-project-opened carries only the isNew signal, not a hydration trigger.

Rationale: isNew is already computable at the call site — project.id == project_id (the freshly generated UUID) tells us whether the INSERT won or the ON CONFLICT branch fired. No schema change, no fat aggregate query, no removed working code.

title: Queue Advisor architecture mismatch: agent-spawn vs Claude API proxy
description: Protocol.md §6 specifies the Queue Advisor as a direct Claude API streaming proxy (advisor_chat_start/send/stop via Tauri Channel). The code implements it as an agent-spawn approach: start_advisor_session, respond_to_advisor, get_advisor_turns — using the same poe:advisor wire events and SQLite advisor_turns table as the orchestrated advisor agent. These are architecturally different: the spec uses a direct API call with a streaming Tauri Channel; the code uses a spawned Claude process with poe:advisor events. Both approaches can work but they require different frontend components, different backend commands, and different session lifetime management. Recommend: FIX DOC to reflect the agent-spawn approach already implemented, as it reuses the existing poe:advisor event pathway cleanly.

title: fix: feature and epic nodes never close — execution phase stuck in running forever
description: Feature and epic nodes are organisational containers in the WBS hierarchy — db_find_ready_tasks correctly excludes them from dispatch. But when all their children complete, nothing closes them. In the wordle_004 run all 12 tasks completed but 9 features and 3 epics remained permanently pending. The execution phase (c4a6faea) showed status='running' indefinitely because its member nodes never reached terminal state. Fix: add a post-task-completion hierarchy sweep. When any node reaches terminal state (complete or cancelled), walk upward via parent_id: check if all siblings are terminal — if so, close the parent, then repeat for the parent's parent. Depth is shallow in practice (task → feature → epic). Key design invariants: (1) parent_id is the organisational/context hierarchy — it is intentionally separate from edges which express technical execution dependencies. The sweep walks parent_id only, never edges. (2) check_phase_completion is called at each level of the sweep — after closing a feature, epic, or any top-level task. This handles phases whose direct members include both hierarchy-managed nodes and top-level lifecycle tasks (CONOPS, Guardrails, Plan Increment) that have no parent_id. check_phase_completion is cheap and idempotent so calling it multiple times is safe.
notes: DOC UPDATE REQUIRED before close: (1) Architecture.md — add node lifecycle section documenting the parent_id hierarchy sweep: when a node completes, the orchestrator walks upward via parent_id closing containers whose children are all terminal. Document explicitly that parent_id is organisational context and edges are technical dependencies — these are intentionally separate relationships. (2) Flows.md — update phase completion section to show hierarchy sweep as the primary close path for feature/epic nodes, with check_phase_completion called at each level as a safe idempotent finaliser. Tests required: integration test creating epic → feature → task hierarchy, completing the task, and asserting feature and epic both auto-close and phase gate advances.

title: Route raw agent transcript to per-agent file, not console
description: Currently all agent output — including full JSON transport payloads — is written to stderr alongside orchestrator and ingester diagnostics. In a busy session the raw transport lines (which can contain 1000-token plan outputs) make it nearly impossible to triage errors. Fix: append each raw line from an agent's stream to {project}/.poe/agent_stream/{agent_id}.jsonl as it arrives. The console (stderr) should only emit [orchestrator], [event_ingester], and [agent_lifecycle] diagnostic lines — no [transport] raw: lines. This gives a durable per-agent transcript for post-session inspection while keeping the console signal-to-noise ratio high.

title: Prevent infinite skill-author retry loop on broken agent
description: The dedup guard in dispatch_task only checks for pending and running skill-author nodes. If a skill-author agent emits poe:done without emitting poe:skill (broken agent), the blocked tasks unblock, load_skill fails again, and a new skill-author task is created — producing an unbounded retry loop. Fix options: (1) add a max-retry counter on skill-author nodes (e.g. retry_count >= 3 → mark failing tasks as failed with a clear error), or (2) check whether the skill file already exists on disk before creating a new skill-author task. The fix must also handle the case where the skill file was written but is invalid/unreadable.

title: E2E test: self-healing skill synthesis loop
description:
Verify the complete self-healing loop works end-to-end:

(1) Open a test project and create a task whose skill_id is set to a non-existent skill (e.g. 'foo-missing').
(2) Start a run. Confirm the orchestrator does NOT cancel the task — it stays pending.
(3) Confirm a skill-author task is created with title 'Synthesize missing skill: foo-missing' and dispatched.
(4) Confirm the skill-author agent produces a valid poe:skill event and the file .poe/skills/foo-missing.md is written.
(5) Confirm the previously-blocked task is now dispatched and runs successfully using the newly authored skill.
(6) Run the scenario a second time with the same missing skill — confirm only one skill-author task is created (dedup guard fires).

Test should cover both the rust unit level (dispatch_task logic) where possible and an integration run.

title: Per-stage concurrency: configurable agent concurrency ceiling per workflow stage

Per-stage concurrency limits encode this policy explicitly rather than relying on DAG dependencies alone, and prevent a surge of ready nodes from overwhelming concurrency limits unexpectedly. Inspired by Symphony's max_concurrent_agents_by_state (SPEC.md §8.3).

title: Workspace isolation: each DAG node execution runs in a dedicated git worktree
description: Each DAG node execution gets an isolated git worktree — a full checkout of the repo in a separate directory — so agents can't interfere with each other or with the user's working tree. Worktrees are created on first run and reused for retries. Lifecycle hooks (before_run, after_run) from POE.md run in the worktree context. The agent CWD is always validated to be inside the worktree root before launch. On completion, the agent emits poe:decision with a diff summary, triggering a merge-agent that reviews and executes the merge. The approval gate defaults to human-confirmed before merge runs — as the merge agent proves itself, the gate can be loosened to fully autonomous. Inspired by Symphony's workspace isolation model (SPEC.md §9) adapted for git-native workflows.
design: New workspace_manager module in src-tauri/. git worktree add/remove via std::process::Command. Workspace key sanitization: [A-Za-z0-9._-] only, replace others with _. CWD validation before agent launch in agent_lifecycle. Hook execution via bash -lc with timeout from POE.md hooks.timeout_ms (default 60000). New merge-agent SKILL.md in skills/: receives branch name, diff summary, base branch; resolves conflicts; merges; escalates via poe:decision on conflict. Approval gate is a POE.md field (workspace.merge_gate: manual|auto|conflict-only). Progression path: manual → conflict-only → auto as confidence grows. Depends on Feature 1 (POE.md) for hooks config and merge_gate setting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each DAG node gets a worktree at <workspace_root>/<sanitized_node_id>/
- Worktree is created via git worktree add if it doesn't exist; reused if it does
- before_run and after_run hooks from POE.md execute in the worktree directory
- Agent CWD is validated == worktree path before launch (path traversal protection)
- Worktree path must be inside workspace_root (Symphony Invariant 2)
- On poe:done, agent emits poe:decision with diff summary (files changed, insertions, deletions)

- Merge agent resolves conflicts if any; escalates via poe:decision if it cannot merge cleanly

- workspace_root configurable in POE.md (default: <project_root>/.poe/workspaces/)
- Approval gate configurable in POE.md: manual (default), auto-merge, or conflict-only

title: Continuation turns: multi-turn agent execution on a single thread without prompt resend
description: When an agent completes a turn but the DAG node is not yet done, POE2 continues on the same Claude thread using only lightweight continuation guidance — not the full initial prompt. This matches how humans work: you don't re-read the entire brief every time you pick up a task. Without this, each turn incurs full context reconstruction cost and loses conversation history. Inspired by Symphony's within-worker turn loop (SPEC.md §7.1, §12.3). PREREQUISITE BUG: Lifecycle agents are spawned with session_id: None at all three spawn sites in lifecycle/mod.rs (lines 751, 824, 870). This means resume_workflow() in project.rs always fails with 'has no session_id — cannot resume'. The advisor pattern is the correct reference implementation: generate Uuid::new_v4() before spawning, pass as session_id: Some(uuid) to spawn_agent_internal, stored in workflows table at INSERT time, read back by resume_workflow. Fix is three lines — add Uuid::new_v4().to_string() at each spawn site. This must land first before continuation turn orchestration can be built on top.
design: STEP 1 (bug fix — do this first): In spawn_step_agent, spawn_step_agent_with_prompt, and the task agent spawn in lifecycle/mod.rs, replace session_id: None with session_id: Some(Uuid::new_v4().to_string()). The Uuid crate is already in scope (used by advisor.rs). The workflows table already has the session_id column (dag/mod.rs:301), the INSERT already writes it (dag/mod.rs:883), and resume_workflow already reads it (project.rs:492). Nothing else changes for the bug fix. STEP 2 (continuation orchestration): Add continuation_prompt field to SKILL.md frontmatter. Add turn_count to running node state in dag_store. After each successful turn, agent_lifecycle re-evaluates node completion (poe:done event received?). If incomplete and turn_count < max_turns_per_node, call resume_workflow with continuation_prompt on same session. Use --resume <session_id> path already implemented in agents.rs. Watchdog timer (bp6-ns7.2) resets on each streaming token, not just turn boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- First turn of a DAG node sends the full rendered prompt from POE.md template
- Subsequent turns on the same node send only continuation_prompt (configurable in skill spec)
- The same conversation thread_id is reused across continuation turns
- agent_lifecycle re-checks node completion state after each turn before deciding to continue
- max_turns_per_node is configurable (default 10) to prevent runaway loops
- If max_turns is reached without completion, the node fails with TurnLimitExceededEvent
- Continuation prompt has access to {{attempt}} and {{turn}} template variables
notes: PREREQUISITE RESOLVED (commit 64367ed): All three lifecycle spawn sites in lifecycle/mod.rs now generate Uuid::new_v4() for session_id at spawn time. Workflow records are stored with valid session UUIDs, making resume_workflow() functional for lifecycle agents. Remaining work is the continuation orchestration layer: continuation_prompt in skill spec, turn_count tracking in dag_store, and the re-check loop in agent_lifecycle.

title: POE: automate decision_handoff_harness — replace browser step with scripted response
description:
The decision_handoff_harness tests the poe:decision → human response → --resume flow. Currently it does this via a browser/xterm.js PTY bridge that requires a human to type. This is not needed — we can inject the response programmatically.

## What the test proves

1. Agent runs via stream-json → emits poe:decision + poe:yield → exits
2. Session ID is captured
3. Human response is delivered to the resumed session
4. Agent continues → emits poe:done

The xterm.js/browser is only the production UI mechanism for step 3. For testing, we can skip it.

## Automation strategy

Replace Phase 2 (PTY + browser) with a scripted stream-json resume:

  // Phase 2 — no PTY, no browser. Feed response directly as a resume bundle.
  let resume_bundle = format!("---\nHuman: My scripted response to the decision\n");
  let lines = run_agent_capturing(&resume_bundle, Some(&session_id), &cwd, None)?;
  // Assert poe:done appears in lines

run_agent_capturing() in agent_lifecycle/mod.rs already supports resume_session_id. Use that.

## Implementation

1. In decision_handoff_harness.rs, remove: PTY spawn, WebSocket server, HTML page, open_browser(), 60-second timeout.
2. Replace Phase 2 with: spawn JsonStreamTransport::run() with --resume <session_id> and bundle = 'Human: {scripted response}'
3. Phase 3 (the final stream-json resume asserting poe:done) can be merged with Phase 2, or the test restructured to show the two-stage resume pattern clearly.
4. The test should run in CI without --ignored (remove the #[ignore] guard once automated).
5. Keep the manual xterm.js version in a comment block or doc note for reference.

## Files

- poe2/src-tauri/tests/decision_handoff_harness.rs — primary change
- poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs::run_agent_capturing() — confirm it supports resume_session_id

## Note on session_handoff_harness

That harness tests the actual browser/xterm.js UX end-to-end. Keep it manual — it is correctly marked #[ignore]. The automation here targets the protocol correctness test only.
close_reason: Removed PTY/WebSocket/browser machinery from decision_handoff_harness. Phase 2 now injects the human response as a stream-json resume bundle. #[ignore] removed — test runs in CI.

title: POE Attempt 2 - Phase 4: Skills Uplift
description:
Uplift POE2's agent capabilities by learning from oh-my-claudecode (OMC). Three waves of work emerged from a structured analysis comparing OMC's shell-layer architecture against POE2's process model.

**Wave 1 — New specialist skills (no OMC runtime required)**
OMC patterns adapted as autonomous POE2 agent skills — .md files in poe2/src-tauri/skills/ that emit poe: events per doc-POE/Protocol.md §2. Three new skills fill genuine gaps in the existing library: security-analyst (OWASP + Rust/Tauri review), code-analyzer (deep codebase investigation via poe:review), external-researcher (parallel external doc research via poe:review). A fourth task enhances the existing product-manager skill with the multi-reviewer consensus loop from OMC ralplan, using poe:review to senior-engineer and architecture-analyst before finalising the plan.

**Wave 2 — OMC Runtime-Dependent (POE2-native when the value justifies it)**
ralph, ultraqa, team, sciomc, ultrawork, autopilot. These skills depend on tmux, ask-codex/ask-gemini CLIs, and the OMC session model. **Decision: POE2 will not adopt the OMC runtime.** These patterns will only be built if and when the value justifies native implementation inside POE2's own architecture — as poe: events, skill .md files, and orchestrator behaviour, not as wrappers around OMC's shell layer. No work in this epic.

**Wave 3 — Protocol and skill enhancements (POE2-native)**
Four targeted improvements grounded in doc-POE/Protocol.md and doc-POE/Architecture.md:

1. **poe:skill event**: Agents can write a project-local skill override during task execution by emitting poe:skill. Extends Protocol.md §2 event catalogue. event_ingester writes to {project}/.poe/skills/, which is already the project-level priority tier in skills/mod.rs. Closes the self-improvement loop without manual prompt authoring.

2. **operational-analyst completeness self-scoring**: Before emitting poe:done, the operational-analyst checks whether all 11 CONOPS sections are substantive. Gaps trigger targeted poe:decision rounds. Formalises what good analysts do informally. No new lifecycle stage — the CONOPS stage is the stage. poe:decision thread mode in the queue (UX-Brief.md §Conversational Queue Items) already renders multi-round elicitation correctly.

3. **Skill frontmatter model field**: Add YAML frontmatter parsing to skills/mod.rs (currently load_skill() returns raw markdown). Extract an optional model: field from frontmatter, expose it on ResolvedSkill, and pass it as --model to the claude spawn in agent_lifecycle/mod.rs. title: POE: Fix watchdog liveness — remove AgentHandle from registry on PTY EOF
description: The 7fi.1 watchdog uses Arc::strong_count to detect agent exit, but PTY EOF never removes the AgentHandle from the AgentState registry map. The strong count never drops to 1 so the watchdog runs forever for crashed/completed agents. Fix: in the PTY reader thread, after the BufReader lines loop exits (EOF), remove the agent_id from the AgentState handles map. This naturally drops the AgentHandle's Arc references, the strong count falls to 1, and the watchdog exits on its next poll. Also ensures the registry does not leak handles for finished agents.
